title: Salivary gland ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the salivary glands near your ears and under your jaw: their size, structure, and any stones.
why: For swelling near the ear or under the jaw, pain while eating, a dry mouth, or a lump you can feel.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: If you had salivary gland stones
If you had an ultrasound or CT scan before. Bring the reports
If you have a dry mouth or dry eyes

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Sometimes
prepare.text: You may be asked not to eat for 1 to 2 hours, or be given lemon juice. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: No high collars. Better to take off earrings and necklaces.

bring: Past ultrasounds and reports, if you have them
steps: You lie on your back with your head turned to one side
Gel is put on the skin near your ear and under your jaw
The probe is moved over the skin
Sometimes you are given sour juice and the glands are checked again
The gel is wiped off with a tissue
feel: Cool gel and light pressure from the probe
after: The report is usually ready right away
If needed, the doctor will suggest more tests

faq.a: Sour taste makes the glands work harder. That helps the doctor see the ducts and stones better.

faq.q: Does it hurt if the gland is inflamed?
faq.a: The probe pressure may feel a bit unpleasant. Tell the doctor, and they will be gentler.

reminders.text: Salivary gland ultrasound tomorrow. Check if you should avoid eating before it.
